Write the next round of a bundle, for some of its models

Source: R/hpc.R
next_hpc_round.Rd

Writes a new bundle that fits again some of the models of a bundle written by write_hpc_bundle() (or of an earlier round), with new settings of the sampler and of the jobs: typically the models that did not meet the sampling rule, given more draws or a smaller step. The round is a bundle of its own, in a new folder, copied to the cluster and run with the same scripts as the first.

Usage

next_hpc_round(
  dir,
  models,
  new_dir = NULL,
  ...,
  time = NULL,
  mem_per_cpu = NULL,
  email = NULL,
  remote = NULL,
  rtft_source = NULL,
  template = "alliance"
)

Arguments

dir

A character string, the folder of the bundle the round follows: the first bundle, or the latest round.

models

A character vector, the names of the models to fit again, as in the column model of the first bundle's table of models.

new_dir

An optional character string, the folder to write the round into. It is created if it does not exist, and must be empty if it does. NULL (the default) writes it beside dir, named after the first bundle and the number of the round: round 2 of "my-run" into "my-run-round-2", and round 3, written from that, into "my-run-round-3".

...

The settings of the sampler that change, among chains, iter, warmup, thin, seed, control and init.

time, mem_per_cpu, email

Optional settings of the jobs that change, as in write_hpc_bundle(). NULL (the default) keeps those of the bundle before.

remote

An optional character string, where on the cluster to copy the round, as in write_hpc_bundle(). NULL (the default) takes the bundle's, with its last folder renamed as the round's folder is (scratch/my-run becomes scratch/my-run-round-2).

rtft_source

An optional character string, where the cluster installs rTFT from, as in write_hpc_bundle(). NULL (the default) takes the bundle's.

template

A character string, the scripts of the round, as in write_hpc_bundle().

Value

The path of the round, invisibly. A message says what was written and what to do next.

Details

Everything that makes the results of the rounds comparable is copied from the bundle before, never chosen again: the data (the file itself), the unit left out in cross-validation, the folds, the observation mode and the sampling rule, as well as the account, the modules and the R library of the cluster, where the bundle is copied to (with the round's own folder name) and where rTFT is installed from. With cross-validation by refitting, each model of the round is refitted on the same folds, starting from its new fit. collect_hpc(), given the folders of every round, keeps for each model the result of its latest round.

Every round holds the whole table of models of the first bundle, and fits those named in models, so a model left out of one round can be fitted again in a later one: a round can name any model of the first bundle, whichever round it is written from.

Only the settings of the sampler and of the jobs can change, since anything else would make another model: chains, iter, warmup, thin, seed, control and init in ..., and time, mem_per_cpu and email. A setting not given is kept from the bundle before; control is merged into the bundle's own, so that control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99) keeps a max_treedepth given before. To change a prior, write a new bundle with write_hpc_bundle(). The settings are one set for every model the round names, so a model that needs more draws and one that needs a smaller step are two rounds.

The round must be written by the version of rTFT that wrote the first bundle (and, between releases, from the same commit), so that every round fits the models with the same code.

See also

write_hpc_bundle(), which writes the first bundle, and collect_hpc(), which assembles the results of every round.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# the model "exp_weibull" of the bundle "my-run" did not meet the convergence
# rule: fit it again with more draws and a smaller step, and longer jobs
# (written into the folder "my-run-round-2", beside "my-run")
next_hpc_round("my-run", "exp_weibull", iter = 4000,
               control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99), time = "24:00:00")

# once the results of both are copied back
out <- collect_hpc(c("my-run", "my-run-round-2"))
} # }
